question: Find $k$ if $\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\1&k&2\\1&3&4\end{vmatrix}=0$. Verify the obtained value by direct substitution.
explanation:
Expansion of the determinant
Expanding along the first row, $$\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\1&k&2\\1&3&4\end{vmatrix}=1(4k-6)-1(4-2)+1(3-k)$$
Algebraic simplification
Thus, the determinant is $$4k-6-2+3-k=3k-5$$
Application of the zero condition
Using $3k-5=0$, we obtain $$k=\frac{5}{3}$$
Verification
Substituting $k=\frac{5}{3}$ in the simplified determinant gives $$3\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)-5=5-5=0$$
Hence, the required value is $k=\frac{5}{3}$.
